newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 8.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:

* At least 57 banks are likely to be liquidated, while the licences of 50 others will be revoked due to mismanagement after the companies failed to follow a call from monetary authorities for troubled banks to merge or be acquired in order to improve the performance of the sector, Bisnis Indonesia reported.

* The Dow ended up 33.48 points at a record 6,600.66 on Tuesday, surpassing Monday's record of 6,567.18 with the market partly benefited from the so-called "January effect," a period when stocks are boosted by a flow of cash into mutual funds from corporated bonus payments, dividend distributions and annual retirement account contributions.
* Supporters of ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri demonstrated in Jakarta and Surabaya on Tuesday demanding the right to run in May general elections.
* The Jakarta Composite Index rose 6.41 points, or 0.98 percent, to close at 660.37 points on Tuesday after active buying almost across the board by both foreign and local investors.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,362.90/63.10 in early trading against the opening of 2,362.60/63.10.
* Small-sized Bank Pikko on its debut on Wednesday.
* Astra Internasional after an announcement that the automobile conglomerate had launched new models of its popular Kijang van.
* Hotel Prapatan on market talk that a business tycoon was likely to buy a large stake in the company.
* Textile firm Mayertex following an announcement of a tender offer plan by privately-owned PT Ciptawira Binamandiri.
* Property firm Summarecon on market talk that the firm was likely to acquire another property firm and announce a rights issue.
